memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "From the blue, purple and scarlet yarn they made woven garments for ministering in the sanctuary. They also made sacred garments for Aaron, as the Lord commanded Moses." - Exod 39:1 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The chapter opens with clothing, and the last phrase sets the tone for everything that follows: "as the Lord commanded Moses."

You will meet that phrase again and again in this chapter — it appears more than a dozen times. Scripture is hammering one point: they did it God's way.

Notice what the garments were for. Not display, not status, but "ministering in the sanctuary." These were working clothes for service in God's presence.

And notice they were made for Aaron — the man who had shaped the golden calf only weeks before. God does not merely forgive Aaron; He clothes him and puts him back to work. Grace restores people to usefulness, not just to safety.

There is something here for anyone who feels their past disqualifies them. Peter denied Christ three times and was restored at a charcoal fire and told to feed the sheep (John 21:15-17). Paul called himself the worst of sinners and then said he was shown mercy precisely so that Christ's patience might be displayed (1 Tim 1:15-16).

A priest could never approach God in his own clothes. Neither can we. We come clothed with Christ (Gal 3:27), wearing a righteousness we did not weave.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Does your past make you feel unusable to God?
2. Do you approach God in your own righteousness or in Christ's?
3. Where are you tempted to serve God your own way rather than His?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, thank You that You clothe failures and send them back to serve. I come dressed in Christ, not in myself. Amen.
